Grown in the lush hills surrounding Lake Kivu in western Rwanda, this coffee comes from smallholder farmers delivering to the Kanzu washing station. Sitting at high elevation (around 1,800–1,900 meters), the region’s volcanic soils and cool climate support slow cherry maturation, enhancing sweetness and complexity.
Processed as a natural, the cherries are dried whole on raised beds, allowing sugars from the fruit to deeply infuse the seed. This results in a cup that leans fruit-forward with a round, syrupy sweetness—balanced by subtle florals and a cocoa-like finish. The profile is expressive yet approachable, showcasing Rwanda’s elegant take on natural processing.

Tasting Notes: Chocolate Fudge, Raisin, Brown Sugar

Sugar cane ethyl acetate or commonly known as EA decaf is a natural process of decaffeinating coffee. It is usually found in Colombia where sugar cane is readily available and starts with making molasses from sugar cane. Once created, it sits in vats to ferment. The bacteria produce acetic acid, much like fermenting coffee, and at the peak of fermentation, alcohol is added to make something called ethyl acetate. For it to be applied to coffee first, the green coffee is steamed in tanks to elevate the moisture level — the beans swell, which allows the extraction of caffeine. Ethyl acetate is added to the mixture, and it dissolves the caffeine in the coffee. The coffee is then washed with water and laid to dry. In theory, the coffee should reach the same moisture content as it arrived in, which is somewhere between 11-12%. The most important part of EA coffee, and why it tastes so sweet, is it avoids high pressure and high heat, which degrades coffee quickly. Origin: Rwanda
Variety: 
Process: Natural
Roaster: Onyx Coffee Lab
Tasting notes: Dried apricot, cantaloupe, agave, bitter sweet chocolate

Grown in the lush hills surrounding Lake Kivu in western Rwanda, this coffee comes from smallholder farmers delivering to the Kanzu washing station. Sitting at high elevation (around 1,800–1,900 meters), the region’s volcanic soils and cool climate support slow cherry maturation, enhancing sweetness and complexity.
Processed as a natural, the cherries are dried whole on raised beds, allowing sugars from the fruit to deeply infuse the seed. This results in a cup that leans fruit-forward with a round, syrupy sweetness—balanced by subtle florals and a cocoa-like finish. The profile is expressive yet approachable, showcasing Rwanda’s elegant take on natural processing.

Grown in the lush hills surrounding Lake Kivu in western Rwanda, this coffee comes from smallholder farmers delivering to the Kanzu washing station. Sitting at high elevation (around 1,800–1,900 meters), the region’s volcanic soils and cool climate support slow cherry maturation, enhancing sweetness and complexity.
Processed as a natural, the cherries are dried whole on raised beds, allowing sugars from the fruit to deeply infuse the seed. This results in a cup that leans fruit-forward with a round, syrupy sweetness—balanced by subtle florals and a cocoa-like finish. The profile is expressive yet approachable, showcasing Rwanda’s elegant take on natural processing.

Grown in the lush hills surrounding Lake Kivu in western Rwanda, this coffee comes from smallholder farmers delivering to the Kanzu washing station. Sitting at high elevation (around 1,800–1,900 meters), the region’s volcanic soils and cool climate support slow cherry maturation, enhancing sweetness and complexity.
Processed as a natural, the cherries are dried whole on raised beds, allowing sugars from the fruit to deeply infuse the seed. This results in a cup that leans fruit-forward with a round, syrupy sweetness—balanced by subtle florals and a cocoa-like finish. The profile is expressive yet approachable, showcasing Rwanda’s elegant take on natural processing., Herbs & Sun dried tomato muffin

Origin: Rwanda
Variety: Bourbon
Process: Natural
Roaster: Onyx Coffee Lab
Tasting notes: Dried apricot, cantaloupe, agave, bitter sweet chocolate

Grown in the lush hills surrounding Lake Kivu in western Rwanda, this coffee comes from smallholder farmers delivering to the Kanzu washing station. Sitting at high elevation (around 1,800–1,900 meters), the region’s volcanic soils and cool climate support slow cherry maturation, enhancing sweetness and complexity.
Processed as a natural, the cherries are dried whole on raised beds, allowing sugars from the fruit to deeply infuse the seed. This results in a cup that leans fruit-forward with a round, syrupy sweetness—balanced by subtle florals and a cocoa-like finish. The profile is expressive yet approachable, showcasing Rwanda’s elegant take on natural processing.

Origin: Rwanda

Process: Natural
Roaster: Onyx Coffee Lab
Tasting notes: Dried apricot, cantaloupe, agave, bitter sweet chocolate

Grown in the lush hills surrounding Lake Kivu in western Rwanda, this coffee comes from smallholder farmers delivering to the Kanzu washing station. Sitting at high elevation (around 1,800–1,900 meters), the region’s volcanic soils and cool climate support slow cherry maturation, enhancing sweetness and complexity.
Processed as a natural, the cherries are dried whole on raised beds, allowing sugars from the fruit to deeply infuse the seed. This results in a cup that leans fruit-forward with a round, syrupy sweetness—balanced by subtle florals and a cocoa-like finish. The profile is expressive yet approachable, showcasing Rwanda’s elegant take on natural processing.

region n the east and the Rwenzori Mountains in the west. Grown in the lush hills surrounding Lake Kivu in western Rwanda, this coffee comes from smallholder farmers delivering to the Kanzu washing station. Sitting at high elevation (around 1,800–1,900 meters), the region’s volcanic soils and cool climate support slow cherry maturation, enhancing sweetness and complexity.
Processed as a natural, the cherries are dried whole on raised beds, allowing sugars from the fruit to deeply infuse the seed. The profile is expressive yet approachable, showcasing Rwanda’s elegant take on natural processing.

Grown in the lush hills surrounding Lake Kivu in western Rwanda, this coffee comes from smallholder farmers delivering to the Kanzu washing station. Sitting at high elevation (around 1,800–1,900 meters), the region’s volcanic soils and cool climate support slow cherry maturation, enhancing sweetness and complexity.
Processed as a natural, the cherries are dried whole on raised beds, allowing sugars from the fruit to deeply infuse the seed. This results in a cup that leans fruit-forward with a round, syrupy sweetness—balanced by subtle florals and a cocoa-like finish. The profile is expressive yet approachable, showcasing Rwanda’s elegant take on natural processing., Filter - Daily Selection (Regular)

Origin: Rwanda

Process: Natural
Roaster: Onyx Coffee Lab
Tasting notes: Dried apricot, cantaloupe, agave, bitter sweet chocolate

Grown in the lush hills surrounding Lake Kivu in western Rwanda, this coffee comes from smallholder farmers delivering to the Kanzu washing station. Sitting at high elevation (around 1,800–1,900 meters), the region’s volcanic soils and cool climate support slow cherry maturation, enhancing sweetness and complexity.
Processed as a natural, the cherries are dried whole on raised beds, allowing sugars from the fruit to deeply infuse the seed. This results in a cup that leans fruit-forward with a round, syrupy sweetness—balanced by subtle florals and a cocoa-like finish. The profile is expressive yet approachable, showcasing Rwanda’s elegant take on natural processing.

Grown in the lush hills surrounding Lake Kivu in western Rwanda, this coffee comes from smallholder farmers delivering to the Kanzu washing station. Sitting at high elevation (around 1,800–1,900 meters), the region’s volcanic soils and cool climate support slow cherry maturation, enhancing sweetness and complexity.
Processed as a natural, the cherries are dried whole on raised beds, allowing sugars from the fruit to deeply infuse the seed. This results in a cup that leans fruit-forward with a round, syrupy sweetness—balanced by subtle florals and a cocoa-like finish. The profile is expressive yet approachable, showcasing Rwanda’s elegant take on natural processing.

Origin: Rwanda
Variety: Bourbon
Process: Natural
Roaster: Onyx Coffee Lab
Tasting notes: Dried apricot, cantaloupe, agave, bitter sweet chocolate

Grown in the lush hills surrounding Lake Kivu in western Rwanda, this coffee comes from smallholder farmers delivering to the Kanzu washing station. Sitting at high elevation (around 1,800–1,900 meters), the region’s volcanic soils and cool climate support slow cherry maturation, enhancing sweetness and complexity.
Processed as a natural, the cherries are dried whole on raised beds, allowing sugars from the fruit to deeply infuse the seed. This results in a cup that leans fruit-forward with a round, syrupy sweetness—balanced by subtle florals and a cocoa-like finish. The profile is expressive yet approachable, showcasing Rwanda’s elegant take on natural processing.

Country: Colombia
Region: Huila
Variety: Caturra, Castillo, Colombia
Processing: Fully Washed, E.A. Processed Decaf
Tasting Notes: Chocolate Fudge, Raisin, Brown Sugar

Sugar cane ethyl acetate or commonly known as EA decaf is a natural process of decaffeinating coffee. It is usually found in Colombia where sugar cane is readily available and starts with making molasses from sugar cane. Once created, it sits in vats to ferment. The bacteria produce acetic acid, much like fermenting coffee, and at the peak of fermentation, alcohol is added to make something called ethyl acetate. For it to be applied to coffee first, the green coffee is steamed in tanks to elevate the moisture level — the beans swell, which allows the extraction of caffeine. Ethyl acetate is added to the mixture, and it dissolves the caffeine in the coffee. The coffee is then washed with water and laid to dry. In theory, the coffee should reach the same moisture content as it arrived in, which is somewhere between 11-12%. The most important part of EA coffee, and why it tastes so sweet, is it avoids high pressure and high heat, which degrades coffee quickly. This allows the natural terroir flavors to come through, making it a sweet and bright decaf., Spindrift Sparkling Water (Regular), Nitro Iced Coffee - Nitrogen infused iced coffee

[Fruit] KANZU NATURAL (Regular) - [FRUIT] KANZU NATURAL
Origin: Rwanda
Variety: Bourbon
Process: Natural
Roaster: Onyx Coffee Lab
Tasting notes: Dried apricot, cantaloupe, agave, bitter sweet chocolate

Grown in the lush hills surrounding Lake Kivu in western Rwanda, this coffee comes from smallholder farmers delivering to the Kanzu washing station. Sitting at high elevation (around 1,800–1,900 meters), the region’s volcanic soils and cool climate support slow cherry maturation, enhancing sweetness and complexity.
Processed as a natural, the cherries are dried whole on raised beds, allowing sugars from the fruit to deeply infuse the seed. This results in a cup that leans fruit-forward with a round, syrupy sweetness—balanced by subtle florals and a cocoa-like finish. The profile is expressive yet approachable, showcasing Rwanda’s elegant take on natural processing.

Origin: Rwanda
Variety: Bourbon
Process: Natural
Roaster: Onyx Coffee Lab
Tasting notes: Dried apricot, cantaloupe, agave, bitter sweet chocolate

Grown in the lush hills surrounding Lake Kivu in western Rwanda, this coffee comes from smallholder farmers delivering to the Kanzu washing station. Sitting at high elevation (around 1,800–1,900 meters), the region’s volcanic soils and cool climate support slow cherry maturation, enhancing sweetness and complexity.
Processed as a natural, the cherries are dried whole on raised beds, allowing sugars from the fruit to deeply infuse the seed. This results in a cup that leans fruit-forward with a round, syrupy sweetness—balanced by subtle florals and a cocoa-like finish. The profile is expressive yet approachable, showcasing Rwanda’s elegant take on natural processing.

[Fruit] KANZU NATURAL (Regular) - [FRUIT] KANZU NATURAL
Origin: Rwanda
Variety: Bourbon
Process: Natural
Roaster: Onyx Coffee Lab
Tasting notes: Dried apricot, cantaloupe, agave, bitter sweet chocolate

Grown in the lush hills surrounding Lake Kivu in western Rwanda, this coffee comes from smallholder farmers delivering to the Kanzu washing station. Sitting at high elevation (around 1,800–1,900 meters), the region’s volcanic soils and cool climate support slow cherry maturation, enhancing sweetness and complexity.
Processed as a natural, the cherries are dried whole on raised beds, allowing sugars from the fruit to deeply infuse the seed. This results in a cup that leans fruit-forward with a round, syrupy sweetness—balanced by subtle florals and a cocoa-like finish. The profile is expressive yet approachable, showcasing Rwanda’s elegant take on natural processing., [Bright] BENJAMIN PAZ SL28 (Regular) - [BRIGHT] BENJAMIN PAZ SL28
Origin: Honduras
Variety: SL28
Process: Washed
Roaster: Onyx Coffee Lab
Tasting notes: Orange, Black tea, Raisin, Juicy

Grown in the mountains of Santa Bárbara, this lot comes from renowned producer Benjamin Paz at La Salsa farm, one of Honduras’ most celebrated coffee producers, with multiple Cup of Excellence recognitions. Sitting around 1,600 meters, the high elevation slows cherry development, building complexity and sweetness.
This SL28 variety—more commonly found in Kenya—brings a unique profile to Honduras, combining East African–style brightness with Central American depth. Carefully processed using a dry-fermented washed method and dried on raised beds, the result is a clean, structured cup with vibrant acidity, layered fruit, and a refined, caramel-like finish.

Origin: Rwanda
Variety: Bourbon
Process: Natural
Roaster: Onyx Coffee Lab
Tasting notes: Dried apricot, cantaloupe, agave, bitter sweet chocolate

Grown in the lush hills surrounding Lake Kivu in western Rwanda, this coffee comes from smallholder farmers delivering to the Kanzu washing station. Sitting at high elevation (around 1,800–1,900 meters), the region’s volcanic soils and cool climate support slow cherry maturation, enhancing sweetness and complexity.
Processed as a natural, the cherries are dried whole on raised beds, allowing sugars from the fruit to deeply infuse the seed. This results in a cup that leans fruit-forward with a round, syrupy sweetness—balanced by subtle florals and a cocoa-like finish. The profile is expressive yet approachable, showcasing Rwanda’s elegant take on natural processing., [Bright] BENJAMIN PAZ SL28 - Whole bean coffee (Regular) - [BRIGHT] BENJAMIN PAZ SL28
Origin: Honduras 
Variety: SL28 
Process: Washed
Roaster: Onyx Coffee Lab
Tasting notes: Orange, Black tea, Raisin, Juicy 

Grown in the mountains of Santa Bárbara, this lot comes from renowned producer Benjamin Paz at La Salsa farm, one of Honduras’ most celebrated coffee producers, with multiple Cup of Excellence recognitions. Sitting around 1,600 meters, the high elevation slows cherry development, building complexity and sweetness.
This SL28 variety—more commonly found in Kenya—brings a unique profile to Honduras, combining East African–style brightness with Central American depth. Carefully processed using a dry-fermented washed method and dried on raised beds, the result is a clean, structured cup with vibrant acidity, layered fruit, and a refined, caramel-like finish.

Grown in the lush hills surrounding Lake Kivu in western Rwanda, this coffee comes from smallholder farmers delivering to the Kanzu washing station. Sitting at high elevation (around 1,800–1,900 meters), the region’s volcanic soils and cool climate support slow cherry maturation, enhancing sweetness and complexity.
Processed as a natural, the cherries are dried whole on raised beds, allowing sugars from the fruit to deeply infuse the seed. This results in a cup that leans fruit-forward with a round, syrupy sweetness—balanced by subtle florals and a cocoa-like finish. Grown in the lush hills surrounding Lake Kivu in western Rwanda, this coffee comes from smallholder farmers delivering to the Kanzu washing station. Sitting at high elevation (around 1,800–1,900 meters), the region’s volcanic soils and cool climate support slow cherry maturation, enhancing sweetness and complexity.
Processed as a natural, the cherries are dried whole on raised beds, allowing sugars from the fruit to deeply infuse the seed. This results in a cup that leans fruit-forward with a round, syrupy sweetness—balanced by subtle florals and a cocoa-like finish. The profile is expressive yet approachable, showcasing Rwanda’s elegant take on natural processing.

Grown in the lush hills surrounding Lake Kivu in western Rwanda, this coffee comes from smallholder farmers delivering to the Kanzu washing station. Sitting at high elevation (around 1,800–1,900 meters), the region’s volcanic soils and cool climate support slow cherry maturation, enhancing sweetness and complexity.
Processed as a natural, the cherries are dried whole on raised beds, allowing sugars from the fruit to deeply infuse the seed. This results in a cup that leans fruit-forward with a round, syrupy sweetness—balanced by subtle florals and a cocoa-like finish. The profile is expressive yet approachable, showcasing Rwanda’s elegant take on natural processing.

Origin: Rwanda
Variety: Bourbon
Process: Natural
Roaster: Onyx Coffee Lab
Tasting notes: Dried apricot, cantaloupe, agave, bitter sweet chocolate

Grown in the lush hills surrounding Lake Kivu in western Rwanda, this coffee comes from smallholder farmers delivering to the Kanzu washing station. Sitting at high elevation (around 1,800–1,900 meters), the region’s volcanic soils and cool climate support slow cherry maturation, enhancing sweetness and complexity.
Processed as a natural, the cherries are dried whole on raised beds, allowing sugars from the fruit to deeply infuse the seed. This results in a cup that leans fruit-forward with a round, syrupy sweetness—balanced by subtle florals and a cocoa-like finish. The profile is expressive yet approachable, showcasing Rwanda’s elegant take on natural processing.

Grown in the lush hills surrounding Lake Kivu in western Rwanda, this coffee comes from smallholder farmers delivering to the Kanzu washing station. Sitting at high elevation (around 1,800–1,900 meters), the region’s volcanic soils and cool climate support slow cherry maturation, enhancing sweetness and complexity.
Processed as a natural, the cherries are dried whole on raised beds, allowing sugars from the fruit to deeply infuse the seed. This results in a cup that leans fruit-forward with a round, syrupy sweetness—balanced by subtle florals and a cocoa-like finish. Origin: Rwanda
Variety: Bourbon
Process: Natural
Roaster: Onyx Coffee Lab
Tasting notes: Dried apricot, cantaloupe, agave, bitter sweet chocolate

Grown in the lush hills surrounding Lake Kivu in western Rwanda, this coffee comes from smallholder farmers delivering to the Kanzu washing station. Sitting at high elevation (around 1,800–1,900 meters), the region’s volcanic soils and cool climate support slow cherry maturation, enhancing sweetness and complexity.
Processed as a natural, the cherries are dried whole on raised beds, allowing sugars from the fruit to deeply infuse the seed. This results in a cup that leans fruit-forward with a round, syrupy sweetness—balanced by subtle florals and a cocoa-like finish. The profile is expressive yet approachable, showcasing Rwanda’s elegant take on natural processing.
